Vacancy by expiry: election before the term ends. Casual vacancy (death, resignation, removal): filled **as soon as possible** – **no six-month deadline**; the new VP gets a **full 5-year term**.
The Constitution is **silent** on who performs the VP's duties during a vacancy; the **Deputy Chairman** performs only the duties of the **Chairman of the Rajya Sabha**.

On a **vacancy** in the President's office (death, resignation, removal) the VP **acts as President until a new President is elected** and enters office – a **maximum of six months**, because **Art. 62** requires the election **within six months** of the vacancy.
When the President is **absent, ill or unable**, the VP **discharges his functions** until he resumes.

While acting he gets the **powers, immunities and emoluments of the President**; he does **not perform the duties of Chairman of the Rajya Sabha** (the **Deputy Chairman** presides) and draws no Chairman's salary.

If both offices are vacant (e.g. the acting VP resigns), the **Chief Justice of India** (then the senior-most SC judge) discharges the President's functions – **President (Discharge of Functions) Act, 1969**.
